newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Persistent dollar demand by local and offshore players drove the rand through key chart points on Thursday to leave it two cents weaker at its worst level in a month.
At the 1400 GMT finish, the rand was quoted at 4.5315/5365 against the dollar from a previous 4.5110/5160 finish and after touching a day's worst level of 4.5350 bid about an hour before the close.
The rand was last above the 4.53 level on August 27.

Dealers said a combination of local importer and London- and German-based dollar demand as well as the breach of key resistance levels provided the catalyst for the rand's break out of its recent 4.48 to 4.52 range.
"We've seen demand for three days straight out of London, Germany and from local importers," a dealer said.
The fall of technical resistance at 4.5250 also triggered demand, while the dollar's resurgence against the Deutschmark and the yen also contributed to the local currency's woes.
In spite of the weight of negative factors depressing the rand, dealers said they expected the rand's renewed fall to be short-lived.

"Some people are talking 4.55 as the next level, but I don't think it will go as weak as that," one trader said. "The bond and money markets are holding their own which is a good indications that things are a lot more stable than we have seen in the past."
He said those two factors augured well for a return to the 4.48 to 4.52 range seen in recent weeks.
Against the crosses, the rand eased to 7.0798/0921 on sterling from 7.0543/0666 on Wednesday, but firmed to 0.3353/3358 marks from 0.3342/3350 marks previously.
The bond market was left relatively unscathed by events on the currency market as a stronger U.S. Treasury bond market neutralised the effects of the weaker rand.
"We had one or two quick moves...the rand weakening on the dollar had a bit of an impact and we spiked up to 15.16 (percent)," a dealer said.
"But then the U.S. figures came out and helped the market back," he added.

A 3.1 percent month-on-month fall in U.S. durable goods orders in August provided a fillip for gains on the Treasury bond market where the yield on the benchmark 30-year T-bond fell to 6.88 percent from 6.93 percent overnight.
At the finish, the key local R150 bond was at 15.12 percent from 15.10 percent overnight.
Dealers said the market would take direction on Friday from the release of preliminary August money supply is due late on Friday.
Economists are predicting year-on-year M3 growth to increase to 15.7 percent from July's 14.69. Growth in private sector credit extension is seen slowing to 17.9 percent from 18.50 in July.
August trade figures are also scheduled for release either on Friday or next week.
Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net sellers of 140.7 million rand worth of South African bonds on Wednesday after selling 5.77 million rand on Monday.
Nominal cumulative volumes amounted to 2.82 billion rand on Wednesday from 10.45 billion rand on Monday.
On the money market, three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.70 to 15.90 percent, while 90-day BAs were unchanged at 15.15 to 15.30 percent.
The Reserve Bank quoted the daily shortage lower at 6.989 billion rand on Wednesday from 7.301 billion rand on Monday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
